**Donor stewardship** is the process of nurturing and maintaining long-term relationships with donors after they make a gift to a nonprofit organization. It focuses on building trust, showing appreciation, demonstrating the impact of their contributions, and engaging them through personalized communication to encourage repeat giving and increased support over time.

### Key Elements from Definitions Across Sources
| Source | Core Definition |
|--------|-----------------|
| [CCS Fundraising](https://www.ccsfundraising.com/insights/donor-stewardship-best-practices/) | Relationship-building via consistent communication, personalized engagement, and demonstrated impact. |
| [Bonterra Tech](https://www.bonterratech.com/blog/donor-stewardship) | Post-gift nurturing to acknowledge gifts, invite involvement, and connect via preferred channels, aiming for ongoing, growing support. |
| [Blackbaud](https://www.blackbaud.com/industry-insights/glossary/what-is-donor-stewardship) | Consistent communication, gratitude, and engagement to make donors feel valued, informed, and connected to the mission. |
| [FreeWill](https://www.nonprofits.freewill.com/resources/blog/donor-stewardship) | Post-gift relationship-building with acceptance, acknowledgment, recognition, and reporting to inspire loyalty and future gifts. |
| [EAB](https://eab.com/resources/blog/advancement-blog/4-stewardship-principles-deepen-donor-relationships/) | Personalized efforts to make donors feel seen, valued, and appreciated, turning one-time gifts into lasting support. |
| [Dormie Network Foundation](https://www.dormienetworkfoundation.org/resource-center/stewardship-ideas) | Extending relationships beyond the gift through recognition, appreciation, management, and retention. |
| [Aly Sterling](https://alysterling.com/donor-stewardship/) | Systematic outreach to deepen emotional connections, immersing donors in the mission for frequent, larger gifts. |
| [ADRP](https://www.adrp.net/assets/documents/adrpdefinitionsexpanded.pdf) | Fiduciary management of gifts per donor intent, often overlapping with donor relations to show high-quality interactions and outcomes. |

### Why It Matters
Stewardship is the longest phase of donor cultivation, transforming transactions into mutually beneficial partnerships. It boosts retention (e.g., repeat donors give more), fosters trust, and can lead to larger gifts, multiyear commitments, or network introductions, as noted in sources like [Candid](https://candid.org/blogs/donor-stewardship-tips-building-enduring-funder-relationships/). Effective practices include timely thank-yous, impact updates, and involvement opportunities, starting immediately after a gift.
